To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the amount of newly-synthesized [(14)C]-labeled acetylcholine (ACh) accumulated in a particulate fraction isolated from PC12 cells was not affected by increasing the expression of VAChT, the vesicular acetyl choline transporter; and (2) the effectiveness of the vesamicol in reducing the filling of the vesicular fraction with newly synthesized ACH was reduced by increasing the expression level of VAChT.
the vesicular acetyl-choline transporter (VAchT) does not regulate the vesicular release or uptake of newly synthesized acety-choline in PC12 pheochromocytoma cells.

overexpression of VAchT does not increase the amount of newly syntheized [(14)C]-ACh that accumulates into synaptic vesicles, and that vesamicol is less effective at blocking the filling of synaptic vesicles with newly synthesized [(3)H]-ACh when the vesicular transporter is overexpressed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism(s) by which the vesicular neurotransmitter transporter regulates neurotransmitter release from presynaptic nerve terminals.
the mechanisms that regulate the vesicular release and uptake of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine (ACh).
the mechanisms that control the vesicular release and recycling of ACh from synaptic vesicles in neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uptake of ACh is not regulated at a level of its uptake by vesicles.
the vesicular transport of ACh is not regulated by the amount of VAchT protein associated with PC12 cells.
vesamicol inhibits vesicular ACh uptake, but does not inhibit the vesicular release process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VAChT is not a rate-limiting component of the vesicular release mechanism of PC12 cells.

the amount of VAchT protein present in a PC12 cell does not regulate either the amount of newly synthetized [(14)C]-acetylcholine acquired by that cell's synaptic vesicles or the release of that newly synthetized ACh from those synaptic vesicles.
VAChT is a necessary but not sufficient component of the machinery for the vesicular release and uptake of ACh in PC12 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vesamicol is not a good tool for studying the regulation of ACh uptake by VAChT.
the uptake of [(3)H]-ACh by the vesicular transporter is a very rapid process and that it does not require ATP.
VAChT is not the limiting step in the release of ACh by PC12 cells.
